New: a VPN in the notch. An OpenVPN client with nothing else to install: AI Notch carries OpenVPN 2.7.8 and a small helper that runs it. It is off until you install the helper in Setup.

What's new

- VPN chip: a VPN chip in the footer, beside Prod and RAM. Green with the profile's name while connected, amber while connecting or reconnecting, red after a failure, grey when off.
- VPN panel: a row per profile with Connect, Disconnect or Cancel; connected, its address, how long, and the traffic both ways. Log shows OpenVPN's last lines.
- Signing in: the notch never takes typing, so a username and password, a private key's passphrase or a one-time code is asked in a small window under the notch. Static and dynamic challenges ask for the code there; a sign-in page (SSO) opens in your browser. Remember the password keeps it in your login Keychain.
- Dropped connection: a connection that was up and ended without Disconnect shows a red crossed lock in the collapsed notch and notifies, also while the screen is unlocked, since traffic stopped going through the VPN.
- A connection keeps running when the notch closes or AI Notch quits.

Set up

1. Setup → VPN → Install… asks for your admin password once. The helper copies itself, OpenVPN and OpenVPN's macOS DNS script to /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/info.ankeshshiv.notch.vpn/ and starts as a launch daemon. OpenVPN needs root for the tunnel, routes and DNS; the helper runs it only for your user.
2. Import Profile… (in Setup or the VPN panel) takes an .ovpn file from your VPN provider or admin.
3. Click the VPN chip, then Connect.

What a profile may hold

OpenVPN runs as root, so each profile is checked when imported. It is refused when it would run a program (up, down, route-up, plugin, script-security), load code (engine, providers), read or write a file by path (ca /path, auth-user-pass /path, log, status, config), or take over the helper's own settings. Certificates and keys must be inline (<ca>…</ca>, <cert>, <key>, <tls-crypt>), as exported profiles usually have them. Windows-only lines (block-outside-dns, register-dns) are left out. To check a profile first:

    /Applications/AINotch.app/Contents/Helpers/ai-notch-vpnd check ~/Downloads/work.ovpn

Known limits

- OpenVPN 2.7 only (no IKEv2, WireGuard or tap devices), one connection at a time.
- BF-CBC and other ciphers of OpenSSL's legacy provider are not available.
- If OpenVPN is killed outright (not through Disconnect), the DNS it set stays until the next connection or a network change.
- The helper serves the user who installed it; other users on the Mac cannot use it.
- Uninstalling the app does not remove the helper: click Setup → VPN → Remove first, or afterwards run `sudo /Library/PrivilegedHelperTools/info.ankeshshiv.notch.vpn/ai-notch-vpnd uninstall`.

Install or upgrade:

    brew install --cask ankeshshankar/tap/ai-notch
    brew upgrade --cask ai-notch

After an upgrade, open AI Notch again and click Set Up to put the hooks back.

First open: the app is signed ad hoc and not notarized, so macOS blocks it once. Open AI Notch, then in System Settings → Privacy & Security click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. If Set Up then reports the helper is blocked, run the command it shows:

    xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/AINotch.app

Requires macOS 15 or later. OpenVPN is GPLv2; its licence and where its source is are in AINotch.app/Contents/Resources/OpenVPN.
